subject: data-science
intro: Data science leads into the quantitative professions that turn raw data into decisions: data scientists, statisticians, actuaries and operations research analysts — and the survey researchers who generate the data first.

roles.title: Data Scientists
roles.what: Develop and implement analytics techniques that transform raw data into meaningful information, applying data mining, data modelling, machine learning and visualisation software to large structured and unstructured datasets, then reporting the findings.
roles.where: The whole workflow is this course: Python programming and tables, visualisation, sampling and empirical distributions, hypothesis testing, inference for regression and classification, ending in updating predictions.

roles.title: Statisticians
roles.what: Develop or apply mathematical and statistical theory and methods to collect, organise, interpret and summarise numerical data into usable information, in specialisms from biostatistics to business and economic statistics.
roles.where: Units 9 through 14 — randomness, sampling and empirical distributions, testing hypotheses, comparing two samples, estimation and why the mean matters — are the inference toolkit the job runs on.

roles.title: Actuaries
roles.what: Analyse statistical data on mortality, accident, sickness, disability and retirement rates to construct probability tables that forecast risk and liability for future benefits, and set the insurance rates and reserves required.
roles.where: The probability, hypothesis-testing and estimation units teach the risk arithmetic actuaries perform; the prediction and inference-for-regression units extend it to forecasting long-horizon liabilities.

roles.title: Operations Research Analysts
roles.what: Formulate mathematical models and optimising methods that produce information for management decision-making and policy formulation, including optimal time, cost and logistics networks for programs and operations.
roles.where: The classification unit trains the modelling mindset — build a predictor, measure its error — while the causality units teach separating signal from confounding before advising decision makers.

roles.title: Survey Researchers
roles.what: Plan, develop or conduct surveys; analyse and interpret the meaning of survey data, determine survey objectives, and suggest or test question wording, including supervising survey teams.
roles.where: Causality and experiments plus sampling and empirical distributions teach why a sample can and cannot stand for a population — the core of survey design — and testing hypotheses covers reading the results.
